lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Tuesday's Town Council work session, where the comp plan, gondola subcommittee, and — most consequentially — a third-party audit of the Town's rental housing policies all come up for review; that last piece directly shapes who can afford to stay here. Wednesday's County meeting carries real weight too, with the BOCC set to ratify an income-eligibility shift at Pinion Park to 80% AMI, quietly redrawing who qualifies for a deed-restricted unit.
